\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{LLM-judge reliability on seven semantic dimensions (EXP4). Original
cohort: ICC on the $n=147$ fully-rated cases, Krippendorff's $\alpha$ on
$n=192$ cases (see text). Replication: a second panel of three judges on the
same 192 cases, all fully rated; primary (label-hidden) condition, ICC with
its 95\% confidence interval. ICC(1,1) = one-way random-effects single-rater
model. No dimension reaches the $\geq 0.75$ good-reliability threshold
(Koo and Li, 2016) in the primary condition of either cohort.}

\small
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
                       & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Original cohort} & Replication \\

\midrule
Clarity                & 0.321    & 0.278 & $-0.019$ [$-0.160$, 0.123] \\
Concision              & 0.453    & 0.409 & 0.373 [0.244, 0.489] \\
Actionability          & 0.400    & 0.362 & $-0.025$ [$-0.166$, 0.117] \\
Audit Usefulness       & 0.376    & 0.340 & 0.699 [0.619, 0.765] \\
Completeness           & 0.585    & 0.566 & 0.731 [0.657, 0.791] \\
